title: Debugger — Overview and definition
body: Signature edition. Original Signature implementation approach, labeled Signature throughout. Signature edition. Original Signature implementation approach, labeled Signature throughout. The Debugger is one of the 100 writing programs and tools AI should have: the actual programs, software tools, and engines — code editors, compilers, document creators, testing tools — that let an AI create real documents and working software. The key distinction this database honors: a description of a debugger is not itself a debugger. So this record carries the ACTUAL working implementation — real code, executed at build time, with verified outputs recorded below.

body: Signature edition. Original Signature implementation approach, labeled Signature throughout. Signature edition. Original Signature implementation approach, labeled Signature throughout. Inputs to the debugger: the data structures the implementation consumes, documented in the code. Outputs: the transformed result, verified by the demos. Error contract: invalid inputs produce structured errors, never silent corruption. The demos on this page exercise the contract on valid inputs, edge cases, and invalid inputs alike.
